description: Curated canonical reference library deconstructing flagship RightMotion clips by creative strategy. Teaches the creative reasoning, composition architecture, and temporal choreography rather than raw implementation duplication.

references.title: Distraction Noise (The Cost of Switching)
references.whyItIsStrong: Communicates the abstract cognitive penalty of context switching using a single, intuitive horizontal conduit that sags under discrete physical weights, slowing flow speed live on screen.
references.primaryVisualIdea: Each interruption physically drops onto an attention beam, causing cumulative deflection and slowing the traveling focus pulse until single-tasking resets it to zero.
references.visualMechanism: Live SVG quadratic bezier deflection curve driven by spring-staged load drops, with a travelling flow pulse whose velocity is inversely coupled to deflection.
references.compositionStrategy: Centered minimalism with generous vertical breathing room. The conduit spans the horizontal axis (y=920); a single minimal percentage readout sits above it; zero clutter.
references.cameraStrategy: Static locked camera with subtle entrance scale. Lets the physical motion and deflection command 100% of viewer attention without camera motion noise.
references.temporalStrategy: Stepwise escalation: each spoken word beat drops a new node, culminating in severe strain at 14s, followed by an immediate, decisive elastic rebound and color shift to emerald at 17s.
references.whyItRemainsClear: Strict 3-tier hierarchy: exactly one primary mechanism (conduit), at most one supporting cue (capacity %), and pristine luminous ground with zero competing elements.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: How to represent an abstract mental tax as a live physical load; how to couple flow velocity to mechanical strain; how to make the resolution snap feel earned.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Do not hardcode identical coordinates for unrelated clips; adapt the physical mechanism to what the new script actually means.

references.title: Structural Pressure (Why Small Pressures Break Us)
references.whyItIsStrong: Visually proves that duration, not mass, causes burnout: a single modest 1.0 KG weight never changes size, yet the monolithic architectural slab beneath it sags and fractures as time advances.
references.primaryVisualIdea: A constant weight held over progressive durations (1 min -> 1 hr -> 24 hrs -> 72 hrs) forces an architectural stone beam to sag 80px and propagate hairline stress fractures until released.
references.visualMechanism: Closed SVG polygon slab supported on dual pillars and anchored by a foundation datum line, mutating live with downward curvature and branching fracture strokes.
references.compositionStrategy: Architectural grounding. Dual vertical pillars frame the lateral space; the beam spans horizontally; the single weight sits dead center; negative space isolates the system.
references.cameraStrategy: Stationary, objective viewpoint. Gives the monolithic beam monumental physical stability, making its eventual bending and micro-cracking feel alarming.
references.temporalStrategy: Progressive accumulation across discrete time markers synchronized to voiceover timestamps, micro-tremor under chronic load, and an effortless upward spring release on resolution.
references.whyItRemainsClear: Zero unmotivated cards in the mechanism scenes. The viewer's eyes are drawn directly to the center where weight meets stone. Caption rests comfortably below in the bottom safe zone.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: Using an unchanging subject (1.0 KG weight) against a changing substrate (deforming beam) to make a conceptual argument without explanatory paragraphs.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Avoid lifting weights without a narrative reason; the lift must correspond to an explicit spoken action of letting down the load.

references.title: Emotional Distance (Alone in a Crowd)
references.whyItIsStrong: Uses horizontal negative space as an active emotional storytelling medium. The feeling of superficial connection vs painful disconnection is communicated purely by distance.
references.primaryVisualIdea: A solitary node attempts to maintain a performing tether to a dense social cluster; the tether snaps, the physical gap widens to 620px, and the solitary node settles into peaceful self-sovereignty.
references.visualMechanism: Dynamic spatial node choreography: cluster coordinates shift right while solitary node drifts left into empty negative space, coupled with a snapping tension line and dimension caliper.
references.compositionStrategy: Extreme asymmetric spatial tension. The right side contains dense visual activity (the crowd); the left side is wide open negative space. The gap between them is the subject.
references.cameraStrategy: Static wide frame. Moving the camera would destroy the viewer's perception of expanding physical distance between the two subjects.
references.temporalStrategy: Flickering amber tether during the 'performing' phase, sharp shockwave burst at the snap beat (frame 820), wide silent drift, and radiant green radial bloom at resolution.
references.whyItRemainsClear: Minimalist node semantics. The crowd is a tight interconnected geometry; 'YOU' is an isolated circle with a white center dot. Zero decorative filler.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: Treating empty space not as unused canvas, but as the primary emotional carrier; using dimension calipers to make invisible psychological distance measurable.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Do not scatter nodes randomly across the canvas; every spatial position must represent an intentional psychological relationship.

references.title: The Dopamine Sugar Trap (Allostatic Curve)
references.whyItIsStrong: Visualizes physiological and neurochemical deficits using live allostatic curve depletion and biometric tracking.
references.primaryVisualIdea: A biometric curve plunges beneath baseline recovery thresholds under compounding deficit load.
references.visualMechanism: Dynamic biometric graph with threshold breach indicators and biological debt counters.
references.compositionStrategy: Clean cyber-mint on bio-navy canvas with generous spatial isolation.
references.cameraStrategy: Objective data monitoring viewpoint with slight vertical drift.
references.temporalStrategy: Continuous decay leading to critical alarm threshold crossing.
references.whyItRemainsClear: Single biometric curve without extraneous decoration.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: Representing biological debt through live threshold curves.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Avoid floating medical charts that do not interact with spoken timestamps.

references.title: The Threshold Effect (Baseline Recalibration)
references.whyItIsStrong: Demonstrates the subtle erosion of standards through physical baseline displacement: each minor compromise pushes a horizontal datum line downward, where it permanently settles.
references.primaryVisualIdea: A clean horizontal standard datum line is repeatedly struck by descending pressure impulses, sagging and establishing a new, lower tolerated baseline.
references.visualMechanism: ThresholdBoundary with persistent ghost memory: the original standard remains as a faint dashed reference line while the active boundary resets lower.
references.compositionStrategy: Full-bleed horizontal datum line anchored across the canvas center. Visual tension is created entirely by the vertical displacement between original and new baselines.
references.cameraStrategy: Subtle vertical tracking that follows the descending baseline, emphasizing the downward drift.
references.temporalStrategy: Impulse -> Deflection -> Plastic deformation -> Settlement. The rhythm mirrors the psychological process of accommodating what was previously intolerable.
references.whyItRemainsClear: Extreme restraint: one line, one reference ghost, and descending impulse particles. Instant mobile comprehension.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: How persistent ghost memory (dashed lines or faint traces) visually communicates irreversible change without requiring text explanations.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Don't displace lines without leaving ghost traces; the comparison between past and present is what creates the insight.

references.title: Small Compromises (The Carved Pathway)
references.whyItIsStrong: Explains neuroplasticity and habit formation through the physical metaphor of a carved furrow: the first stroke requires immense force, but subsequent strokes glide effortlessly.
references.primaryVisualIdea: A vertical kinetic blade carves a channel into a resistant material plane. High drag and vibration on pass 1; frictionless low drag on pass 2.
references.visualMechanism: KineticFurrow coupled with ResistancePathway: surface deformation where particle speed increases and particle friction sparks decrease with each repetition.
references.compositionStrategy: Vertical split or central channel. The focal furrow cuts through the center of the frame, dividing the before and after states.
references.cameraStrategy: Slow macro push-in along the carved groove, increasing intimacy as the furrow deepens.
references.temporalStrategy: High friction struggle (slow, shuddering velocity, heavy audio clicks) transitioning into fluid, accelerated motion (smooth glide, harmonious tone).
references.whyItRemainsClear: The viewer directly feels the difference in physical resistance between the two passes. Motion quality carries the entire concept.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: Using velocity and friction as narrative variables; contrasting high-drag struggle with frictionless ease.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Do not use generic particle fountains; sparks must physically originate from the contact point between blade and surface.

references.title: The Architecture of Pressure (Fulcrum Equilibrium)
references.whyItIsStrong: Explains why work feels overwhelming not because the tasks are huge, but because the recovery counterweight has been placed too close to the center fulcrum.
references.primaryVisualIdea: A physical seesaw lever beam tilts steeply as demand weights are placed on one end, while a small recovery block fails to balance it until shifted outward for greater leverage.
references.visualMechanism: KineticFulcrumBeam with angular torque simulation: rotation angle is calculated dynamically from mass times distance from center.
references.compositionStrategy: Centered triangular fulcrum wedge supporting a horizontal balance beam. Symmetry establishes equilibrium; asymmetry creates urgent tension.
references.cameraStrategy: Slight camera tilt tracking the beam's angle of deflection to intensify the visceral feeling of imbalance.
references.temporalStrategy: Static equilibrium -> sudden weight placement -> steep angular drop -> repositioning of counterweight -> smooth level restoration.
references.whyItRemainsClear: Everyone intuitively understands a seesaw. The physical mechanics of torque instantly explain why small changes in habit leverage produce huge mental shifts.
references.whatShouldBeLearned: Leveraging universal physical intuition (balance, leverage, gravity) to explain abstract personal dilemmas.
references.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Don't over-complicate the seesaw with decorative brackets or extraneous weight shapes; keep weights clean and geometric.
